name: Trust, But Verify: A Self-Verification Approach to Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
authors: Xiaoyuan Liu, Tian Liang, Zhiwei He, Jiahao Xu, Wenxuan Wang, Pinjia He, Zhaopeng Tu, Haitao Mi, Dong Yu (Tencent; CUHK-Shenzhen; SJTU). Lead affiliation: Tencent (AI Lab / corresponding author Zhaopeng Tu).
venue: NeurIPS 2025 (accepted; OpenReview id gA3fFAEXNT). arXiv preprint arXiv:2505.13445.
reflection_type: learned-critic-model (self-verifier): the policy is RL-trained to critique and score its own on-policy solutions; verification is tool-verified against a rule-based outcome verifier that supplies ground-truth scores. So it combines verbal self-critique with verifiable-reward supervision rather than relying on a separate trained reward model.
feedback_source: verifiable reward from a deterministic rule-based outcome verifier (exact-match correctness of the final boxed answer against ground truth). The same outcome verifier supplies the ground-truth score that supervises the self-verification task, so feedback is environment/ground-truth-oracle based (label-supervised), not purely self-generated.
iteration_structure: online RL training loop (iterative across N PPO iterations). Within each iteration it is a two-stage rollout: (i) generate K solutions per problem, (ii) construct verification prompts from those on-policy solutions and generate K verification critiques; both trajectory types are mixed into one batch for the policy update. At inference it is single-shot (Pass@1) with optional test-time scaling via majority/verification-weighted voting (k=4, k=8).
reflection_object: Two coupled objects are reflected on and modified via weights: (1) the reasoning chain / solution output is improved through problem-solving reward, and (2) the model's own on-policy generated solution is the object of self-verification (the model critiques and scores its own solution). The learning ultimately updates model weights (parametric), so the persistent artifact modified is the policy parameters; no external prompt/skill/memory artifact is produced.
requires_training: RL (online PPO). Implemented with Proximal Policy Optimization (actor + critic, GAE, KL penalty, clipping) on top of Qwen2.5 base models; trained with the verl framework. No SFT or DPO stage in the main method (an SFT baseline is reported separately).
reward_or_critic_model: verifiable reward (rule-based deterministic outcome verifier giving binary/discrete correctness: +1 boxed-and-matched, -0.5 boxed-but-not-matched, -1 unboxed). The same verifier scores both solution generation and self-verification. PPO additionally uses a learned value/critic model for advantage estimation, but the improvement signal itself is a verifiable reward, not a learned reward model. The model also acts as self-as-judge for its own solutions, but that judgment is supervised by the verifiable reward.
distillation_target: model-weights. The self-verification skill is distilled into the policy parameters via the joint RL objective (verification trajectories contribute to the gradient update); there is no separate episodic memory, prompt, or skill-library artifact.
emergent_vs_engineered: Hybrid / engineered-objective with emergent behavior: the joint solve-and-verify RL objective and the verification prompt template are engineered, but the resulting more-frequent and more-accurate in-context self-verification behavior emerges from the RL optimization (verification phrase frequency rises +1.09 for 3B, +1.05 for 7B after training; not prompt-scaffolded at inference). It targets the 'superficial self-reflection' problem of plain RLVR-emergent reflection.
memory_type: short-term/scratchpad (the chain-of-thought reasoning and the verification critique within a response). No persistent long-term or episodic memory store; learned experience is held in model weights.
memory_persistence: within-episode for the scratchpad reasoning/verification; learned capability persists cross-task and cross-session only via the updated model weights (parametric), not via an explicit external memory.
memory_curation_mechanism: n/a — there is no external memory bank to curate. Online verification data is generated fresh each iteration from on-policy solutions and is not stored/accumulated (the ablation contrasts this with an offline/static verification set drawn from a distant policy).
error_localization_granularity: holistic/outcome-level. The verifier judges only final-answer correctness (binary outcome), and the self-verification task asks for a single correctness score for the whole solution rather than localizing the failing step. The natural-language critique can discuss steps, but the reward signal is outcome-level (no step-level/process reward).
intra_task_vs_inter_task: inter-task — learning transfers across the training distribution and to held-out benchmarks via weight updates; the model does not iteratively refine a single answer within one inference (no in-flight retry loop at test time). Each training problem is independent; the acquired solve+verify skill generalizes across tasks.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: avoidance-via-training plus internalized in-flight verification: at training time, errors shape the policy so future solutions/verifications improve (avoidance). The internalized verification can also recompute/recheck within a single reasoning trace (e.g. re-deriving constraints mid-solution), giving some mid-trajectory self-correction, but there is no explicit episodic retry-with-reset mechanism.
task_domains: math (mathematical reasoning). Future work mentions extension to code generation, physics, and other verifiable-reward domains, but experiments are math-only.
benchmarks: Training: MATH-Hard (Level 3-5, 8,523 problems). Evaluation: MATH500, Minerva Math, OlympiadBench, AIME 2024, AMC 2023. Verification accuracy measured on the same benchmarks; off-the-shelf verifier comparison vs Math-Shepherd-7B and GPT-4o.
headline_result: On Qwen2.5 (1.5B/3B/7B) with PPO, RISE jointly improves reasoning Pass@1 and dramatically improves self-verification accuracy. Up to 2.8x increase in verification accuracy over a Zero-RL baseline; RISE-1.5B reaches 74.5% avg verification accuracy vs 26.8% for Zero-RL (+47.7 pts). RISE-3B: 33.5% avg reasoning (vs Zero-RL 32.5%) and 74.3% avg verification (vs 35.8%); reported +3.7% reasoning and +33.4% self-verification over Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct. RISE-7B: 42.9% avg reasoning, 69.2% avg verification.
baselines: Qwen2.5 Base, Qwen2.5 Instruct (instruction-tuned), SFT (on MATH-Hard), and Zero-RL (same RL setup as RISE but without the verification objective). For self-verification: off-the-shelf verifiers Math-Shepherd-7B (discriminative) and GPT-4o (generative). Reference point GPT-4o reported in the main table.
gains_vs_baseline: Vs the strongest comparable baseline (Zero-RL, identical RL setup minus verification objective): reasoning avg gains are small (RISE-1.5B +0.4 pts to 24.4; RISE-3B +1.0 pts to 33.5; RISE-7B +1.2 pts to 42.9), while self-verification gains are large (1.5B +47.7 pts, 3B +38.5 pts, 7B +22.6 pts; up to 2.8x). Test-time: verification-weighted voting adds +0.2% (3B) and +1.9% (7B) over standard majority voting at k=4; RISE-7B 49.8% vs Zero-RL 48.3% at k=8 + self-verify. Self-verified reasoning accuracy gains over Zero-RL: +3.3% (1.5B), +1.7% (3B), +6.5% (7B).
compute_cost_profile: Training: adds a verification rollout+update stage on top of standard RLVR. Default verification batch size 128 = 12.5% of the 1024 generation batch, so roughly +12.5% extra training rollouts/compute over Zero-RL; scaling verification ratio up to 100% further increases compute and keeps improving verification accuracy. Train batch 1024, mini-batch 128, K=8 rollouts/problem, temperature 1.0. Inference: base method is single-pass Pass@1 (no extra cost); optional test-time scaling uses k=4 or k=8 samples plus self-verification scoring (k-fold inference multiplier).
known_limitations: Evaluated only on mathematical reasoning (no code/physics/general domains, left to future work). Only PPO is tested; GRPO/RLOO left to future work. Outcome-level (binary final-answer) verification only — no step-level/process verification, so error localization is coarse. Reasoning accuracy gains over Zero-RL are marginal (the main win is verification skill). Depends on a reliable rule-based outcome verifier and ground-truth answers for training, limiting applicability to non-verifiable domains. No dedicated limitations section in the paper; these are inferred from method scope and future-work discussion.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: external-tool/verifier + oracle-label/ground-truth at training time. Both the problem-solving reward and the self-verification ground-truth score come from a rule-based outcome verifier that requires the ground-truth answer. The learned self-verifier then operates intrinsically at inference (no oracle needed at test time), but the capability is acquired under ground-truth-supervised verifiable reward.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive (without test-time label leakage). The internalized self-verification improves self-verified reasoning accuracy (+3.3/+1.7/+6.5% over Zero-RL) and yields gains from verification-weighted voting at inference using only the model's own scores; RISE self-verifiers also outperform off-the-shelf verifiers (Math-Shepherd-7B, GPT-4o). Reasoning gains are modest but consistently positive, so self-correction is net-positive and does not require an oracle at test time.
calibration_effect: improves — the learned self-verification provides meaningful confidence signals: verification-weighted majority voting beats plain majority voting (+0.2% 3B, +1.9% 7B at k=4), indicating better answer calibration/confidence estimates. Explicit calibration metrics (e.g. ECE) are not reported, so this is improvement on a calibration-proxy rather than a direct calibration measurement.
failure_attribution_capability: classifies-failure-mode (binary correctness judgment of its own solution) — the self-verifier outputs a critique plus a correct/incorrect score for a whole solution. It does not attribute a specific failing step (no step-level localization) or a responsible agent (single-agent setting).
failure_mode_addressed: Directly targets 'superficial self-reflection' (models that nominally reflect/verify but do not robustly catch their own errors) — closely related to MAST-style superficial/ineffective self-verification and reflection failures. The case study shows RISE avoids a plausible-but-wrong verification (Zero-RL 'verifies' the wrong answer 222 by misapplying divisibility rules) by performing genuine multi-step re-derivation (validating 2220).
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new benchmark or trace dataset released. Code released at https://github.com/xyliu-cs/RISE; training uses existing MATH-Hard and evaluation uses existing public benchmarks (MATH500, Minerva, OlympiadBench, AIME24, AMC23).
builds_on: RLVR / Zero-RL for reasoning (DeepSeek-R1, Open-Reasoner-Zero, Zeng et al. SimpleRL-Zoo), PPO (Schulman et al. 2017) with GAE; verifiable-reward training (Lambert et al. Tulu/RLVR); generation-verification gap and self-improvement (Song et al. 2024, Huang et al. sharpening); self-critique signals (Xi et al. 2024, Xie et al. 2025); generative/process verifiers (Math-Shepherd / Wang et al. 2023a, Lightman et al. process reward); self-rewarding / verification-for-self-improvement (Yuan et al. 2024, Xiong et al. 2025); self-play solve-and-test (Lin et al. 2025). Built on Qwen2.5 and the verl framework.
extended_by_or_inspired: Cited by and related to subsequent self-evolving/self-verification RL reasoning work, e.g. R-Zero: Self-Evolving Reasoning LLM from Zero Data (2025), and broader RLVR-with-self-verification follow-ups. (Specific downstream citations are limited given the recency; ~32 citing works as of mid-2026.)
reasoning_model_native: Not specifically targeted at o1/R1-style reasoning models — RISE is the training method that *induces* reflective self-verification in standard Qwen2.5 base models, addressing the 'superficial self-reflection' that plain RLVR-emergent reflection (R1-style 'aha') exhibits. It is complementary to, rather than assuming, a built-in-reflection reasoning model.
on_policy_distillation_link: Strongly on-policy: verification training data is constructed from the model's own on-policy generated solutions each iteration (ablation shows online/on-policy verification is crucial — an offline/distant-policy verification set sharply degrades verification accuracy). This is self-distillation of a verification skill into weights via on-policy RL rather than distillation from a separate teacher; conceptually aligned with on-policy distillation/self-improvement on the model's current output distribution.
sample_efficiency: Self-verification reward rises faster and to a higher level than the problem-solving reward during training (consistent with the generation-verification gap), so the verification skill is acquired sample-efficiently. Main runs trained ~96 PPO steps (offline-comparison policy taken at step 96, the final step); verification accuracy keeps scaling with more verification compute (12.5%->100% of generation batch). Exact total rollout/step counts to reach headline numbers are not fully specified.
